name: Notify employer in writing of when, where and how the injury happened
source_quote: Tell your employer, in writing, when, where, and how you were injured. Do this within 30 days of injury.

name: Tell health care providers the injury is work-related and name the employer's insurer
source_quote: health care providers that you have a work-related injury or illness and give the name of your employer's workers' compensation insurer.

name: File an Employee Claim with the Board
deadline_text: within two years of the injury or illness
source_quote: A claim must be filed within two years of your injury/illness

name: File a Limited Release of Health Information
condition: same body part injured before, or a similar injury
source_quote: If you injured the same body part before, or had a similar injury, you must also file a Limited Release of Health Information (Form C-3.3).

name: Employer notifies its insurer or claims administrator of the injury
condition: lost time beyond the day or shift of injury, or treatment beyond ordinary first aid
source_quote: Employers should notify their workers' compensation insurer or claims administrator immediately of any work-related injury or illness.

name: Employer reports the injury directly to the Board (optional)
condition: only if the insurer or claims administrator does not report on the employer's behalf
source_quote: the employer can notify the Board directly by filing the Employer's Report of Work-Related Injury/Illness (Form C-2F).

name: Insurer or claims administrator reports the injury to the Board
deadline_text: on or before the 18th day after the injury, or within 10 days after the employer learns of it, whichever is greater
source_quote: Insurers or claims administrators must report a work-place injury or illness to the New York State Workers' Compensation Board on or before the 18th day after the workplace injury or illness occurred, or within 10 days after the employer learns of the event

name: Provider files medical reports with the Board and the insurer
source_quote: Your health care provider will file medical reports with the Board and with your employer or its insurer.

name: Attend follow-up medical visits
deadline_text: 15 days after the injury, then every 90 days while lost time continues
source_quote: See your doctor 15 days after the injury and then every 90 days if you have ongoing lost time.

name: Pay lost wage benefits
deadline_text: within 18 days of the accident or 10 days from when the insurer was informed
condition: claimant disabled, case accepted, more than seven days of work missed
source_quote: you will be paid within 18 days of the accident or 10 days from when the insurer was informed.

name: Hold a hearing on a disputed claim
deadline_text: on average 28 days from the date the claim was disputed
source_quote: On average, a hearing will be scheduled 28 days from the date that the claim was disputed.

name: Appeal the judge's decision in writing
deadline_text: within 30 days of the filing date
source_quote: You or your employer's insurer may appeal that decision, in writing, within 30 days of the filing date.

name: Apply for disability benefits while a disputed claim is heard
source_quote: If your case is disputed, you may apply to receive disability benefits while the case is heard.

name: Request reimbursement of medical travel expenses
deadline_text: submit receipts at least every six months
source_quote: Submit receipts for those expenses at least every six months to the Board and to the insurer using the Claimant's Record of Medical and Travel Expenses and Request for Reimbursement (Form C-257)
